instruction: I need assistance converting all uppercase text in my document to title case for a more professional appearance. Please help me with this formatting task.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Converts uppercase text to title case. Verified by checking no all-uppercase text remains and title-cased text is present.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Incorrect title case detection logic - metric accepts sentence case instead of proper title case (text.istitle() or text[0].isupper() accepts 'This is a sentence' instead of requiring 'This Is A Sentence')
CRITICAL: No baseline comparison - evaluator cannot verify conversion actually occurred, only checks final state (document with no uppercase text would pass even if user did nothing)
CRITICAL: Cannot distinguish between successful conversion vs. document already having no uppercase text vs. user deleting uppercase text
ISSUE: Overly permissive title case check - condition 'text[0].isupper() and not text.isupper()' accepts mixed case, sentence case, or any non-uppercase text
ISSUE: No verification of specific content - evaluator doesn't know what text was originally uppercase, cannot verify specific text was converted correctly
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add baseline capture in config to store original document state before user action (e.g., download original file to separate location for comparison)
Fix title case detection: use proper title case logic that checks each word starts with uppercase (e.g., all([word[0].isupper() for word in text.split() if word]) for multi-word text)
Add getter that compares before/after states to verify uppercase text was actually converted to title case
Consider using python-docx text comparison to identify which specific text runs changed from uppercase to title case
Alternative approach: Store expected title-cased content in expected values based on original document analysis
